newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA - ESTONIAN ENERGY AND NRGEN SIGN BUSINESS PLAN.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA - ESTONIAN ENERGY AND NRGEN SIGN BUSINESS PLAN.

text.p: Estonian Energy and NRGen signed a business plan for Narva Power Inc. on Monday, under which 51 percent of the to be established company's shares will belong to Estonian Energy.
Some 49 percent of Narva Power will go to NRGenerating International B.V (NRGen), a wholly owned subsidiary of NRG Energy Inc, the parties said at a news conference after the signing.
"The purpose of the plant is to create a framework to modernise the Eesti and Balti power stations," the managing director of NRG Energy Europe, Robert J.Brown, told the news conference.
An independent auditor, Price Waterhouse, has estimated the value of the two power stations at $70 million.

Proceeding from the agreed distribution of shares, NRGen will contribute cash in the amount of $67.225 million. In addition, NRGen will contribute cash over five years for the financing of social programmes.
The business plan foresees investments of $1.1 billion during the period 1998 to 2027.
The investments are to be funded by equity, reinvestment of profits and borrowings from local and international financial institutions.
The break-even point is estimated in year seven and the business plan comes in force on January 1, 1998, Brown said.
According to the business plan, the proposed price of electricity generated by the plants will range from 0.26 to 0.42 kroons/kWh, compared to present the 0.28 kroons.
Hillar Lauri, the director of NRG Energy in Estonia, added that the proposed price excludes inflation.
A central goal of the business plan is to keep a lid on growing unemployment in North-East Estonia.
